output_json.diff_review: Non-test change is confined to FilenameUtils.getPrefixLength(): the UNC branch computes the candidate prefix length and now only returns it when isValidHostName(filename.substring(2, pos-1)) is true, otherwise NOT_FOUND. Adds four private helpers (isValidHostName, isIPv4Address, isIPv6Address, isRFC3986HostName) plus supporting constants/patterns and four java.util/regex imports — a verbatim match of the official Commons IO 2.7 CVE-2021-29425 patch. No public API signatures change; the only behavioral change is that malformed UNC prefixes (invalid host names) now yield null/-1, which is the intended security behavior. The test change is purely additive: one new testNormalizeUncPathTraversal asserting null for "//../foo", "\\..\\foo", "//../", "//.." and "//foo bar/baz" while keeping "//server/a" and "//127.0.0.1/a" working. No existing tests were weakened. The POV file lives under untracked .security-pipeline/ and is not product code.
output_json.pov_result: Independently reproduced both states via the Docker wrapper. Pre-patch (compiled from git show HEAD original FilenameUtils.java): normalize("//../foo") = "//../foo", VULNERABLE, EXIT=0. Post-patch (current worktree): normalize("//../foo") = null, NOT VULNERABLE, EXIT=1. Matches orchestrator logs. The POV only drives the public FilenameUtils.normalize API and adds no assertions that bypass project code.
output_json.regression_result: mvn -B test -Dtest=FilenameUtilsTestCase passed independently: Tests run: 38, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0. Legitimate UNC paths (//server/a, //127.0.0.1/a) still normalize correctly, confirming no over-broad regression. The 4 unrelated full-suite failures noted by the patcher (FileUtilsCleanDirectoryTestCase, FileFilterTestCase canRead/canWrite) stem from running as root in the container and touch no code changed by this patch.
output_json.summary: The patch applies the upstream Apache Commons IO 2.7 fix for CVE-2021-29425 (CWE-022). FilenameUtils.getPrefixLength() now validates the UNC host-name segment (RFC 3986 reg-name or IPv4/IPv6 literal) so a leading double-separator followed by ".." (e.g. "//../foo") is no longer treated as an inviolable authority prefix; normalize() returns null instead of leaving the ".." traversal segment intact. Independently confirmed the POV flips from VULNERABLE (exit 0, normalize="//../foo") on the original HEAD source to NOT VULNERABLE (exit 1, normalize=null) on the patched tree, and FilenameUtilsTestCase passes 38/38. The fix is minimal and root-cause-focused; the POV was not modified or disabled and legitimate UNC paths still normalize correctly.
